::: {#rem-set-counterexample}
#### Disproving a claim about all sets

A claim of the form "for all sets $A$, $B$, ..., some equation holds"
is disproved by one choice of sets for which it fails (@def-disproof).
Small sets, such as $\emptyset$ and $\set{1}$, are a good place to look.
A Venn diagram (@def-venn-diagram) can suggest where to look:
shade each side, find a region shaded on one side only,
and put an element in that region.

:::
